blocks.text: II. Examination Techniques (Updated 06/26/2024)
blocks.html: II. Examination Techniques (Updated 06/26/2024)

blocks.text: Genitourinary (G-U) includes genital system and urinary system (kidney/bladder/urethra/ureters)
blocks.html: Genitourinary (G-U) includes genital system and urinary system (kidney/bladder/urethra/ureters)

blocks.text: The physical exam does not include a pelvic examination.
blocks.html: The physical exam does not include a pelvic examination.

blocks.text: Genital exam is not required unless indicated by past medical history (PMH) or symptoms (e.g., masses or areas of tenderness). It may be performed at the discretion of the examiner and applicant.
blocks.html: Genital exam is not required unless indicated by past medical history (PMH) or symptoms (e.g., masses or areas of tenderness). It may be performed at the discretion of the examiner and applicant.

blocks.text: III. Aerospace Medical Disposition
blocks.html: III. Aerospace Medical Disposition

blocks.text: (See Item 48., General Systemic, for details concerning diabetes and Item 57., Urine Test, for other information related to the examination of urine). The following tables list the most common conditions of aeromedical significance and course of action which should be taken by the AME, as defined by any corresponding protocol and disposition in the table. Medical certificates must not be issued to an applicant with medical conditions that require deferral, or for any condition not listed in the table that may result in sudden or subtle incapacitation without consulting the AMCD or the RFS. In most cases, medical documentation must be submitted for these condition in order to support an issuance of a medical certificate.
